requirements.evidence: Contract largely present: enums (app/Enums/TicketStatus.php, TicketChannel.php), InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException, Queue/Ticket models with required casts and relations, Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:46), migrations with cascading FKs, unique(['queue_id','code']) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:23-24). IssueTicket rejects negative priority (IssueTicket.php:16), re-reads the queue with lockForUpdate inside the transaction (IssueTicket.php:26-29) and retries up to 5 times on unique violations. nextCode walks tickets by id and keeps the last code matching /^A(\d+)$/ (Ticket.php:71-79), which covers A999->A1000->A1001, skips malformed codes and handles the A002-deletion example. The write-once guard is an updating hook over getDirty (Ticket.php:39-47). call() checks membership, then status, and throws the required exceptions. Weak spots: deleting the most recent ticket (e.g. A003) makes nextCode reuse A003, which contradicts 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'. call() also relies on $user->memberships(), which does not appear in the diff.

conventions.evidence: The change ships no Pest tests, which breaks the 'No production code without a test' rule. Authorization in Ticket::call() is a hand-rolled membership query (Ticket.php:98-104) instead of a policy/gate, although conventions require 'Authorization always goes through policies/gates'. CHANGELOG.md is not updated. Docs are partly synced: business-rules.md gains queue and ticket rules, but the existing line 'immutable after issuance, except called_at and called_by' is left in place next to the new status rule. Positives: the domain write is an Action (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php), $fillable is set deliberately and both migrations have down().

security.evidence: The call path is authorized server-side against entity membership before any write (Ticket.php:98-105), and the ticket is left unchanged when the check fails. Inactive queues are checked against a locked database row, not the stale model (IssueTicket.php:26-29). Fillable is explicit. One limited gap: the authorization check is ad hoc instead of policy-based, so a future caller cannot reuse it through Gate.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: no tests for nextCode edge cases, inactive or stale queue rejection, negative priority, the write-once LogicException, single call, the unauthorized call, or the factory forQueue sequence.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct code with no service layer. nextCode loads every code of the queue on each issuance (Ticket.php:67-69) where reading backwards to the last valid code would do. isUniqueViolation (IssueTicket.php:53-65) mixes SQLSTATE and message sniffing, and 23000 also matches non-unique integrity errors. The factory closure checks isset($attributes['code']) (TicketFactory.php:23-25), which is dead code because an explicit code overrides the closure.

readability.evidence: Clear names and small methods. Minor style inconsistencies: inline FQCNs (\App\Enums\TicketStatus at IssueTicket.php:39, \Illuminate\Database\QueryException at IssueTicket.php:43/53, \RuntimeException at Ticket.php:93) and a redundant same-namespace import 'use App\Models\User;' placed out of order (Ticket.php:13), which Pint's ordered_imports would likely flag.

scope.evidence: Every file in the diff serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, two migrations and the two docs the task asked to update. No HTTP or Livewire code and no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behavior, which breaks the project's mandatory test-first rule and leaves the code-sequence, locking, write-once and call-authorization rules unverified.

nextCode derives the next number from the last remaining ticket, so deleting the most recent ticket (A001..A003, delete A003) makes the next issuance reuse A003, contrary to 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'.
Call authorization is an inline membership query instead of a policy/gate, as the conventions require.
call() depends on $user->memberships(), which is not shown in the diff; if User exposes the relation under another name, call() fails at runtime.
CHANGELOG.md is not updated, and the existing 'immutable except called_at and called_by' sentence now contradicts the added rule that also allows status to change.
nextCode loads every ticket code of the queue on each issuance, so issuance cost grows linearly with queue history.
The unique-violation detection treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (including FK/not-null errors on MySQL) as retryable and also sniffs error messages; a narrower check would be simpler and more accurate.
The isset($attributes['code']) branch is dead code, because an explicitly passed code replaces the closure entirely.
Inline fully qualified class names and a redundant, out-of-order same-namespace import are inconsistent with the file's other imports and likely fail Pint.

review.summary: The change adds the queues/tickets migrations, models, enums, factories, an IssueTicket action with row locking and collision retry, and the write-once and single-call rules. Most of the contract is met with sound logic. However, it ships no tests at all, which breaks a mandatory project convention. Smaller gaps remain: code reuse after deleting the last ticket, ad hoc authorization instead of a policy, and an incomplete docs/CHANGELOG update. It needs substantial rework before approval.
